nodes.title: Constant: clip_skip (when unused, set a value for Image Saver)
Prompt concatenation logic
widgets_values:
**A =** LoRA selected Trigger Words
**B =** Positive w/ Wildcards Extender
**C =** LoRA Manager Prompt
**D =** LLM Final
**E =** Extra + Embeddings
**F =** LoRA names **"Final" Prompt =** A + B + C + D + E Recommended use:
• B: for wildcards expansion only
• C: for the main prompt logic that precedes the LLM text
• E: for quality tags (masterpiece, ...) and Embeddings **Final + F** = Positive Prompt for Image Saver + "Concatenated result" display

nodes.title: LoRA Manager: Prompt node with tag autocomplete (use /character for example)
Single character logic
widgets_values:
When using a character LoRa with trigger words: if your concatenated prompt (includes LLM output) is internally contradictory about who/what the subject is, the model will try to satisfy all the strong subject cues, and the easiest way to do that is to spawn extra character(s). If this happens, copy the result found in the "concatenated result" node (note: when using this solution, remember to disable the LLM nodes) and edit/adapt it into a modified prompt (place the final in the "LoRA Manager prompt"):
ℹ️ Remove additional character reference (he/she) in favor of brief statements. ℹ️ Consider extending the positive prompt with: "solo, single subject, only one person" ℹ️ Also extend the negative prompt with: "extra person, duplicate, two people, crowd" ℹ️ This happens more often in landscape compositions, where the model attempts to fill the blank canvas with the subject.

nodes.title: LLM Positive Prompt
widgets_values:
ℹ️ 01z is a `txt2img` generation step, while 01c is an `img2txt2img` (use an input image and provide a prompt to generate an image).

01c can be used before the main prompt concatenation, while 01z is used after to optimize the final prompt. 

01c: uses QwenVL to analyze an input image and provide a prompt that represents the content of the image for the model to interpret. The system prompt used by the tool is available in the group, adapt as needed.

01z is run after the main prompt is concatenated to optimize the prompt sent to the Sampler. Specific models prefer some form of prompts.

Note: generated prompts can be copied from the the final prompt in 01x and used as-is in the prompt input without needing to re-run LLM generations.

nodes.title: Resolution Master
widgets_values:
The [Resolution Master custom node](https://github.com/Azornes/Comfyui-Resolution-Master) is a powerful tool used to select the initial image resolution. Please refer to its documentation to understand how it can best fit your usage.

In its UI, the top output is the `width`, the next one is `height` and the 4th one is the `batch_size`. 

⚠️ if the surface of the custom node appears blank, this is likely due to a [known incompatiblity with MixLabs](https://github.com/Azornes/Comfyui-Resolution-Master?tab=readme-ov-file#--conflict-with-comfyui-mixlab-nodes). 

If you need a replacement custom node, look at [ComfyUI_ResolutionSelectorPlus](https://github.com/bradsec/ComfyUI_ResolutionSelectorPlus) or [ComfyUI-mxtoolkit](https://github.com/Smirnov75/comfyui-mxtoolkit) "Silder 2D" and add an `Int` for `batch_size`, then reconnect to the existing reroutes (⬆️ top to bottom: `width`, `height`, `batch_size`)

nodes.title: Routing Block + Pipes
widgets_values:
⬇️ This block with most of the workflow links is an aggregation group using the "muter" logic.
 "Any switch" allows the first un-muted entry to provide an input to pass as the node's output. 

We mute unused 🔴 Samplers, so only one is active and is used as the output sent to the later stages.

widgets_values:
The resulting image and its size (before the resize node) is dependent on the selected upscale model. Adapt as needed to match your expectations/available models.

The resize node will in turn make sure the final image match the expected MP resolution.

ℹ️ An AI generated table of upscale models and their usage is added in Stage 3.

nodes.title: VRAM Control **attempts**
widgets_values:
Those bypassers serve as an extra option to attempt to release VRAM (using ComfyUI with an attention CLI parameter is recommended). Note that "yes" means "allow the node to run".
- `Clean VRAM` will **attempt** to release content from the VRAM. This is in addition to how ComfyUI performs its own caching.
- `VRAM Debug` will display the amount of VRAM available to be used. It will also **attempt** to release some as possible. The `Unload all models` below is another toggle available to **attempt** to free additional VRAM.

nodes.title: Narrative + Tags
widgets_values:
You are an expert narrative and bag of words prompt engineer optimized for a fast diffusion transformer that excels at photorealism, anime, artistic styles and complex scenes.

Rules you MUST follow strictly:
- Follow the original prompt's logic: generate what is asked.
- Output ONLY the final prompt: no explanations, no JSON, no thinking trace, no "here is your prompt", no markdown, nothing else.
- First write a concise natural language description (1–3 sentences max). Describe the most important elements of the image in those sentences, and only what is visible: subject(s), and actions; chracters details if present (approx age group, gender expression if clear, hair, facial expression, pose, clothing or lack of, accessories), environment (location type, background elements, time cues); lighting (source, direction, softness/hardness, color temperature, shadows); camera viewpoint (eye-level/low/high, distance) and composition (framing, focal emphasis).
- Then add a very dense, comma-separated tag list emphasizing the most important elements. Use ( ) for slight emphasis, (( )) for stronger, [ ] only rarely if needed for negation.
- Keep total length to under 1024 tokens.
- Prioritize visual impact and composition details for the diffusion model to handle.

Apply those rules to the following original prompt:

nodes.title: Concatenated result
widgets_values: A close-up portrait of a young woman, mid-30s, with long dark hair swept back, serene expression, eyes slightly downcast as she walks forward, draped in a heavy, rich copper uchikake overcoat embroidered with intricate gold kin-komon patterns, her obi featuring a delicate landscape painting, adorned with a small ivory netsuke toggle, stepping through falling sakura petals toward a grand tori gate framed by towering temple pillars, surrounded by shimmering water ripples reflecting muted golden light from above, soft diffused illumination casting gentle shadows across her fabric-clad form, camera positioned low-angle eye level, framing her from chest up against a backdrop of blurred cherry blossoms and misty temple architecture, inkwash texture blending into wetwater effects with sepia undertones and henna accents, evoking depth and motion in every brushstroke.

Write ONE detailed paragraph (6–10 sentences) for a diffusion transformer. 

Rules you MUST follow strictly:
- Describe only what is visible: subject(s) and actions; people details if present (approx age group, action, gender expression if clear, hair, facial expression, pose, clothing, accessories); environment (location type, background elements, time cues); lighting (source, direction, softness/hardness, color temperature, shadows); camera viewpoint (eye-level/low/high, distance) and composition (framing, focal emphasis).
- Be clear in what is detailed to represent settings for characters that would be important to recreate the image for the diffusion model, such as actions or signs.
- Be detailed and direct about visual content; represent in visual terms what the input depicts so that the diffusion transformer can represent it.
- Keep total length to under 2048 tokens.
- Prioritize visual impact and composition details for the diffusion model to handle.
- Output ONLY the final prompt — no explanations, no JSON, no thinking trace, no "here is your prompt", no markdown, nothing else.

nodes.title: 01z: Final Prompt Enhancement
widgets_values:
Perform a prompt enhancement after the last step in 01x and before the first Sampler.
If enabled, the output of this node is the "positive prompt" used.

3 prompts style are available to be selected based on your purpose or the input model (select ONLY 1):
1. Narrative + Tags
2. Narrative
3. Tags

nodes.title: WARNING -- ALWAYS check "Only 1"
widgets_values:
When making any changes to enabled Stages, ALWAYS check that the "Only 1" requirement is met. ⚠️ Enabling disabled Stages WILL enable ALL sub-steps for this stage , breaking the "Only 1" rule.
ℹ️ You will see it happen in the various toggles available in this quick access section as soon as you enable/disable a step. ✅ WHEN this happens, MANUALLY deselect ALL unwanted steps to avoid unawnted steps from being run. ℹ️ "Only 1" groups are set to use `Always One` or `Max One` but this setting is bypassed when the outer group status changes.

nodes.title: Tags
widgets_values:
You are an expert Bag-of-Words (BoW) prompt engineer for Diffusion Transformer models. Your task is to transform an "original prompt" into a dense, comma-separated list of visual tags.

Strict Formatting Rules:
- Output ONLY the tags: No prose, no markdown, no headers, no thinking trace, no explanations.
- Structure: A single, continuous block of comma-separated "unique tags."
- Tag Definition: A unique tag is 1-4 space-separated words (e.g., "lightning arc"). 
- Constraint: Maximum 75 unique tags. NO concepts repetitions (bad: "radiant_sunrise, radiant_sunset, radiant_starfield, radiant_night, radiant_moon, radiant_planets, radiant_aurora, radiant_galaxy, radiant_island, radiant_archipelago, radiant_seas, radiant_mountains, radiant_peaks, radiant_valleys, radiant_graves").
- Weighting Syntax: Use (tag:weight) for emphasis (e.g., (oil painting:1.3)).
- Weight Limits: Range 0.5 to 1.6. Never use 1.0 (BAD: (glowing runes:1.0) OR glowing runes:1.0. GOOD: glowing runes)
- Emphasis Limit: Maximum 10 weighted tags per response.

Content Guidance:
- Literal Interpretation: Describe only what is explicitly requested or logically necessary for the visual (Subject, Appearance, Clothing, Pose, Environment, Lighting, Camera Angle, Style).
- No Abstract/Technical Jargon: Do not use "8k," "masterpiece," "trending on ArtStation," "detailed," or marketing buzzwords.
- Visual Focus: Use concrete nouns and adjectives. If the input is "a girl," specify skin tone, hair color, and clothing only if mentioned or if the style (e.g., Anime) requires specific archetypes.
- Style Integrity: If the input says "Anime," use tags like "cel shaded," "vibrant lineart." If "Photorealistic," use "subsurface scattering," "bokeh," "natural skin texture."
- Token Priority: Order unique tags by importance: [subject], [action/pose], [clothing/appearance], [environment/background], [lighting/atmosphere], [camera/style].

nodes.title: Mode: txt2img vs img2img (Only 1)
widgets_values:
The workflow is able to do `txt2img` or `img2img`.

`txt2img` (01m1) uses "Resolution Master" to set the desired image resolution. Keep the `denoise` to `1.00` since you want to generate a new image from random noise.

Using `img2img` (01m2), provide a source image that will be used as the latent source for the image to be generated from. Set the wanted MP resolution of the initial image (recommended 1.5MP); the node will adapt it based on the shape of the input image. Set the `denoise`: 0.2-0.4 keeps almost everything from the source image, 0.5-0.7 (recommended) balances original composition/shapes with heavy prompt influences, 0.8-1.0 mostly ignore the source image and generate almost entirely from prompt.

Note that it is also possible to use "QwenVL Image 2 Prompt" (01c) to extract a potential prompt from an image.

nodes.title: READ ME FIRST: How to use it
widgets_values:
This is a very simplified version of https://civitai.red/models/2149956/ where I have removed a lot of nodes just to keep the simple initial generation and the initial upscaler (similar to running the much larger workflow without Stage 3 and 4). A lot of the details on usage are in the larger workflow and were not copied here, and a few notes might contain content that is just copied from the larger workflow)

0. Use the various toggle ↘️ to quick select (the arrows at the end of the selection will bring you to the node/subgraph directly).
1. Select a Model to generate an image with, adapts its parameters to match your setup.
2. Decide if you want to perform `txt2img` (enter a prompt and get an image) or `img2img` (use a prompt and a base image to generate a new image based on both). When using `img2img` make sure to provide an image, set the expected base image resolution (in MP) and set a `denoise`.
3. Decide if you want to write your prompt or use use an image and have QwenVL write a prompt (you can still add to the prompt in the main prompting area). When using QwenVL, load an image and select the `preset` for the type of response you need.
4. Decide if you want to use Qwen to optimize the final prompt before the image generation occurs. When doing so, decide on the type of prompt you want generated: tags, narrative or both.
5. Click "Run", the image generation will start with your selected parameters. Depending on the `batch_size` you will have a set of image generated. The final prompt is viewable. After the initial generation, a simple `HiResFix` will upscale the image to 4MP.

Note: an `Image Filter` node is present next to the `Image Saver Positive Prompt` (in green by the image viewer). It will wait one minute and allow you to select the images to send to the upscaler. Mute it to skip it
